sub_themes.sub_theme: grain boundary lithium penetration in garnets

insights.claim: Grain boundaries in LLZO with higher electronic conductivity let lithium be reduced inside the electrolyte.
Blocking-electrode conductivity across grain sizes can separate electronic leakage from mechanical cracking as the shorting cause.
Higher aluminium doping should increase intergranular lithium paths, though doping also confounds grain size.
Wetting interlayers lower interfacial resistance but likely do not prevent internal nucleation at grain boundaries.
Internal lithium deposits present regardless of interlayer, before shorting, would indicate internal nucleation.
CCD variability between identical pellets reflects real defect-driven failure and should be reported as distributions.
Shorting is controlled by the weakest grain boundary path, so CCD should follow Weibull statistics.
Larger electrode areas failing at lower current would show failure is set by vulnerable boundary density.

sub_themes.sub_theme: stack pressure in lithium metal solid-state cells

insights.claim: High stack pressure may mask void formation through lithium creep rather than genuinely improving the interface.
A pressure window exists that maintains contact without forcing lithium into cracks and grain boundaries.
Cells degrading when pressure drops mid-test reveal that pressure was compensating rather than fixing the interface.

sub_themes.sub_theme: operando imaging of lithium dendrite growth

insights.claim: Post-mortem cross sections show only end states and risk preparation artefacts, motivating operando observation.
Side-view optical cells are a stopgap because the polished edge may not behave like the bulk.
Controlled-microstructure samples and failure statistics pair well with an operando tomography group's imaging expertise.

adjacent_ideas.claim: Stack pressure may change the Weibull shape parameter, indicating whether it alters defect populations or only contact.
Dopant segregation strength could set the density of critical defects estimated from area-scaling experiments.
Operando imaging during a pressure step-down could show whether voids or boundary intrusion drive the degradation.
Operando tomography could count internal versus interfacial nucleation events to test weakest-link assumptions directly.
